1	# Conversation extract — the growth pack's conversation-side daily task
2	
3	The conversation-side sibling of [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md): mine this repo's captured
4	conversation logs for durable lessons, post a short summary of the exchange behind each extracted rule on the
5	issue it was worked under, and prune logs past retention. You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue. The
6	access model matches growth-extract — the repo's own content is plain **local git** in the checkout; only the
7	GitHub **issue/PR API** goes through MCP. (Capture, which needs the live session transcript, is the separate
8	in-session step at merge; this task consumes what capture already pushed.)
9	
10	The **method** — the friction signals, the measured efficiency analysis, the lesson bar — stays canonical in
11	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) and is not restated here. The captured log carries what
12	that method needs: per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the tool_use/tool_result pairs behind
13	wall-time numbers.
14	
15	## Conventions used in this doc
16	
17	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for the repo's default branch — substitute whatever it uses.
18	- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for PRs and the issue API.** Reading the
19	  `conversation-logs` branch and its files, staging the `.claudinite/local/packs/` lesson onto a branch, and
20	  the retention prune are all **plain git in this repo's checkout** (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`) — the
21	  branch is *in this repo*, so no cross-repo access is involved, exactly as growth-extract reads `git log` and
22	  stages its lessons. Opening the lesson PR and arming its auto-merge, posting the summary, and the
23	  tracking-issue log go through the session's GitHub MCP tools (`mcp__github__*`) — none of those is a
24	  plain-git operation.
25	- **The repo's local packs.** Everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the canon home repo's own is
26	  `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`; the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` is accepted during the rename
27	  window); never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
28	
29	## The run
30	
31	1. **Fetch the queue.** `git fetch origin conversation-logs`; list its files
32	   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`). No branch, or no `*.jsonl` → stop; a quiet repo is
33	   the common, valid outcome.
34	2. **Read retention.** From this repo's `.claudinite-checks.json`, the grow_with_claudinite entry's
35	   `config.retention_days`. Unset → the prune in step 5 is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). (On a
36	   quiet repo the precondition dispatches only when retention is set *and* the branch's oldest log — by its
37	   filename stamp — is already past it, so a quiet dispatch always has both retention set and something to
38	   prune.)
39	3. **Fresh pass.** For each log captured in the recent window (its filename carries the capture stamp; corpus
40	   dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days): read it
41	   (`git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`) and run the extracting-lessons method over it — including the
42	   wall-time/efficiency analysis, measured from the log's own timestamps, never hand-waved.
43	4. **Route, land, and post.** Fold each keeper into the repo's **own local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`)
44	   at the local promotion ladder's strongest mechanism, exactly as
45	   [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) prescribes — landing the whole run through **one
46	   auto-merging PR** (title `Claudinite growth: conversation extract`, its commit referencing the worked issue
47	   so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes), armed for auto-merge the same way
48	   [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md) delivers: GitHub squash-merges it once the repo's checks pass,
49	   with no human review. For each rule that actually landed, post **one short comment** via
50	   `add_issue_comment` on the issue named in the log's filename (`--issue-<n>--`) — where **`--issue-0--`
51	   means the capture had no associated issue** (a session-end capture), so there is nothing to post on and
52	   the rule simply lands without a comment: one provenance line (the
53	   rule added, the capture date, the session id), then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of
54	   conversation that caused the rule — what was asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule
55	   follows from it. Summarize, never transcribe: the dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue, so no
56	   pasted turns beyond a short quoted phrase, and never the log. A log that yields nothing gets **no**
57	   comment — extraction is the only path to permanence. Finding nothing at all is fine and common.
58	5. **Retention prune.** When `retention_days` is set: for each log whose filename stamp is older than
59	   `retention_days` days, give it a **final hindsight pass** — one last read against the now-current corpus
60	   (steps 3–4 apply to anything it still yields) — then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push
61	   (commit message ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain
62	   add/remove commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
63	
64	## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue
65	
66	The standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract`** in this repo —
67	found by that exact title, never a number; created **closed** if missing; its state never changed afterward.
68	When a run lands a lesson, posts a summary, or prunes logs, log it as one dated comment (via
69	`add_issue_comment`) naming what changed; a run that changed nothing logs nothing.
70	
71	## Run on a capable model
72	
73	Whether a lesson clears the bar — and whether the hindsight pass should overturn a fresh-pass call — is the
74	judgment this task exists for, and its PR auto-merges without a human review gate. This task declares
75	`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
76	
77	## What this task must never do
78	
79	- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits
80	  only.
81	- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
82	  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
83	- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
84	  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
85	- **Never touch the shared canon** — writes go to the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/` (via an
86	  auto-merging PR), its issues, and its logs branch; lifting portable lessons is the central promote task's job.

README.md

1	# Extracting lessons from a working session
2	
3	> **Scope: a single agent ↔ user conversation.** This doc is the **method** for mining one
4	> working session's *dialogue and the actions taken in it* for improvements. It is **not** the
5	> growth extract ([the growth-extract task](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) that mines **issues, PRs, and commits** over repo
6	> history — that routine never sees a conversation. Its two callers: the
7	> [conversation-extract daily task](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md), which applies it to **captured**
8	> conversation logs — where the friction signals below (a clarifying round-trip, a backtrack, a
9	> wait you sat through) survive with their timestamps — and an owner's occasional plain-words
10	> ask for a retrospective over the live session.
11	
12	Portable guidance for mining an agent ↔ user session — a Claude Code web session, a CLI run, a
13	captured conversation log — for durable improvements: read the conversation and convert its
14	friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less dependent on human
15	feedback.
16	
17	Run the reflection on a **capable model.** Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears
18	the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong
19	"lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
20	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model
21	to the judgment it must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the
22	separate efficiency analysis — also live there; this doc is the how-to.
23	
24	## The goal
25	
26	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less
27	rework, less waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but
28	as "where did this cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost
29	next time." If a pass can't name a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's
30	fine (see [No new lessons](#no-new-lessons-is-a-valid--and-common--result)).
31	
32	## When it runs
33	
34	Routinely, in the [conversation-extract daily task](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md) over each captured
35	log (a fresh pass within a day of capture, a final hindsight pass before retention deletes the
36	log) — the standard path. If an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective over the live
37	session, apply the same method and deliver the capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**,
38	never one that self-merges (the nightly auto-merges its own PR per its own doc; a live retrospective
39	wants human eyes). **Never
40	reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner
41	decides when a session is done enough to mine.
42	
43	## What to look for — the friction signals
44	
45	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop
46	cost more than necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
47	
48	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
49	
50	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I
51	meant…"); the agent building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same
52	request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
53	
54	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every
55	question the user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate
56	**convention or glossary entry**; a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first
57	checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc the agent reads cold and gets right the first
58	time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds correctly **without the round-trip**.
59	
60	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
61	
62	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran
63	a command that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light
64	one fit; reinvented something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written
65	to "verify"; missed an existing convention and had it corrected in review.
66	
67	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing
68	helper/convention so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read.** Place
69	it by where the trap is hit, not in a central bucket: a gotcha from **misusing a specific API,
70	class, or library goes as a comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where
71	the next editor of that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list.
72	Co-locate it in a file's own header comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only
73	hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a central gotchas doc for what no single usage site
74	owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant file (a mistake of omission), or a
75	cross-cutting invariant. The test: next time the agent takes the good path first, not after a
76	detour.
77	
78	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
79	
80	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been
81	parallel; a padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its
82	result was already in hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already
83	green.
84	
85	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers and separate the
86	kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting** (sleeps,
87	polling, a finished process not yet killed). A captured log carries per-entry timestamps and
88	per-message token usage, so the numbers are computable, not estimated. A fix is only credible
89	against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
90	was already optimal.
91	
92	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
93	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the
94	subject of the standing **efficiency analysis** in
95	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold a wall-time
96	finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
97	loss of quality.
98	
99	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
100	
101	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks
102	*repeatedly* are a checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how
103	many processes ran — could it be fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its
104	work was done?", stop waiting to be asked — fold those exact questions into a **standing
105	self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the relevant work, and close with a
106	terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each recurring question
107	converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
108	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively,
109	with numbers.
110	
111	## From signal to lesson — the bar
112	
113	A friction signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and
114	generalizable beyond this one session.** Before adding anything:
115	
116	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded
117	  differently, even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
118	- **Route to the local pack that owns it, and prefer the strongest mechanism** — the **local
119	  promotion ladder**, at the project's own level. A project's capture surface is its **local
120	  packs** (`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/`): pick the pack whose territory the lesson belongs
121	  to, then a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in that pack's `rules` (its failure message
122	  *is* the lesson; ship it with a red-first fixture), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a
123	  **pack skill**, and only what neither can carry lands as terse **prose** in the pack's
124	  `RULES.md`. Write more checks and less prose — a check relieves every session's context
125	  completely where prose only relocates it. A gotcha tied to one call site still goes as a
126	  comment at that site (above), not into any pack. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson
127	  warrants segregation, a new local pack is a self-contained directory drop.
128	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared,
129	  cross-project canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote
130	  stage lifts it there centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever
131	  travels.
132	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or
133	  something already implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
134	
135	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
136	
137	Most sessions yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write nothing
138	rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes
139	the canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a
140	genuinely new, reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
141

1 # gcec rules 2 3 The project's standing working rules — injected at session start while this pack 4 is declared. Activity-scoped procedures live in this pack's skills 5 (snapshot-approval, merge-and-ci, testing-guide) and surface on 6 demand; the extractor-automation domain's standing rules are the "Extractor 7 pipeline" section below, and its scheduled tasks live under `tasks/`. 8 9 ## Working rules 10 11 - **Never carry uncommitted edits onto a new branch with 12 `git checkout -- `** — that restores the paths' *committed* 13 content, silently destroying exactly the edits it was meant to preserve. 14 `git checkout -b origin/main` already brings a clean working tree along; 15 when it can't, commit or `git stash` first and never in the same `&&` chain 16 that moves the branch. In #734 the combined one-liner wiped three finished 17 edits **and** invalidated the `check_the_world.mjs` + `npm run test:offline` 18 pass that had just gone green, forcing a full re-verification. 19 - **Cap and qualify every GitHub MCP list/search call** — an unbounded one 20 hard-fails the tool-result cap and costs a 2–3-call dig through the saved 21 result file. `search_issues` handed a bare title string full-text-searches the 22 whole repo and returns every match with its full body: the standing 23 `Claudinite tracker: ` lookup that opens every scheduled task blew up at 24 185–211 KB three times (#734 twice, #753), and `actions_list` without a page 25 cap at 155 KB (#760). Qualify the query (`in:title "Claudinite tracker: 26 "`, or `list_issues` + `labels`) **and** pass a small `perPage` (5–10) — 27 the answer wanted is one issue or one run, never a page of them. 28 - **This repo's one divergence from the canon merge recipe: CI must be green 29 first** — twice for e2e/heavy-browser changes. The project mechanics of driving 30 a merge (dispatching CI in a web session, the poll back-off, when to arm 31 auto-merge instead of waiting) are the merge-and-ci skill — **load it for any PR a session opens**, including one 32 opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended run, not only for a deliberate 33 merge. 34 - **`npm run regen` is the regenerator** (load lists + UI snapshots + 35 generic-coverage baseline/report); a stale artifact can't slip through — its 36 own gate fails. On the `ours` driver (kept in sync with `.gitattributes`): 37 `extension/event-extractors/load-order.generated.json` (from `npm run index`), 38 `dev/requirements//cases/*.png` (from `npm run refresh:ui`), and 39 `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json` 40 + `generic-coverage.GENERATED.md` (from the generic-coverage test). The 41 inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — 42 **not** on the `ours` driver; reconcile via `npm run regen` + the gallery 43 drift gate. If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate 44 firing — review it, don't paper over it. 45 - **Keep divergence small**: when syncing a branch to `origin/main` (by rebase — 46 this repo forbids merge commits), **run `npm run regen`** as part of the sync, 47 so the branch carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest 48 sources. 49 - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), 50 link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — 51 `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` 52 — for one-page review. 53 54 ## Owner commands 55 56 - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for 57 the published artifact. The bump mechanics are the canon `bump-version` 58 skill's; honor an explicit target ("bump version to 1.4.0") or level ("bump 59 patch" / "bump major") when given. Open the PR, 60 get CI green, squash-merge with `(#N)` — 61 saying "bump version" is itself the merge authorization for **this** 62 deterministic bump PR only. The merge triggers **Release: Create Package**; 63 do **not** report done until the `vX.Y.Z` GitHub Release with its refreshed 64 `google-calendar-event-creator.zip` asset is published — poll via the GitHub 65 MCP tools on the merge-and-ci skill's back-off (reporting at merge time races 66 the async build). 67 - **"learned lessons"** = run the canon lessons-learned pass over the current 68 conversation on **the strongest model available**, plus the standing 69 efficiency analysis of the conversation's tool/process usage. Only when the 70 owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. 71 72 ## Testing invariants 73 74 - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads 75 `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every 76 required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct 77 behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a 78 supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. 79 - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** 80 (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the 81 path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate 82 departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction 83 tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live 84 cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared 85 infra (not a test) and stays at the root. 86 - **The pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, 87 currently 2026-06-01) **is the floor of the cases' dates**: author a 88 neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or 89 a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. 90 91 ## Codebase gotchas 92 93 Project-wide footguns only. Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon 94 packs/skills. 95 96 - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the 97 real URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only 98 real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). 99 - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here 100 they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why 101 the worker publishes `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. 102 - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 103 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — 104 strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's 105 user-facing text (the generic extractor's footer-address reader does this, #675). 106 - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it** — the parser 107 auto-closes the `

` and the content lands as its `nextElementSibling`; a 108 `.foo p` selector reads `""` with no error. Bit tel-aviv's description blocks 109 (#602) — read the sibling, not the tag. 110 - **The augment-not-replace + reset-per-load rule lands on `GCal` here** 111 (canon): `registry.js` resets `GCal.sources` on load and is pinned **first** 112 in the load order so it runs before any source pushes (#48, #189). 113 - **`clean()` collapses all whitespace including newlines — single-line fields 114 only.** A description run through it loses every line break (#131, #140, 115 #141); multi-line text goes through the block helpers (`blockText` / 116 `normalizeBlock` / `htmlToText`). Line-break handling is generic, never a 117 per-source choice. 118 - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an 119 event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages 120 (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a 121 mere host match. 122 123 ## Workflow-failure classification 124 125 **Mind the one gap `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` can't see:** it only 126 inspects workflows carrying a `schedule:`, so a workflow that is unattended by 127 some *other* trigger — `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch` — needs its failure 128 job wired by hand. 129 The `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is exactly that shape; its 130 reporters live in the vendored create-package/publish/daily workflows it calls. 131 132 ## Extractor pipeline 133 134 Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the two gcec pack 135 [`tasks/`](tasks/): **create-extractor** (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR 136 adding site support, and the sweep that records a committed `.url`'s missing 137 cached page) and the weekly **generic-extractor-improvements** (read a spec only when working 138 on that pipeline). Adding or refreshing a cached live case by hand is the 139 [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) skill. 140 141 - **All page fetching goes through [`scraperapi.mjs`](tasks/create-extractor/scraperapi.mjs), from a 142 task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** A rendered fetch through 143 ScraperAPI's residential proxy (`render=true`, so a single-page app records 144 post-render HTML with real data). Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the 145 portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the 146 `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' 147 `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and 148 never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 149 vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is 150 the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 151 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 152 event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. 153 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 154 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 155 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 156 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 157 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 158 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 159 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 160 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 161 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 162 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 163 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 164 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 165 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 166 from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 167 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 168 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 169 - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't 170 produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's 171 preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason 172 and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch 173 issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it 174 correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. 175 - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** A 176 removed/renamed case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 177 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 178 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 179 be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers 180 (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). 181 - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — 182 even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call 183 `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see 184 the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` 185 alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every 186 extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's 187 overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its 188 hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction 189 bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, 190 site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating 191 hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the 192 generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a 193 candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in 194 `supportedDomains`). 195 196 ## Architecture rules of the road 197 198 Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update 199 this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is 200 `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): 201 202 - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file 203 per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline 204 itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core 205 generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing 206 from a per-site file. 207 - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs 208 on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over 209 it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page 210 already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a 211 specific site. 212 - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** 213 `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts 214 we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second 215 list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as 216 supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host 217 appears in the list. 218 - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to 219 override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — 220 green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a 221 `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts 222 needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file 223 back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 224 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 225 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 226 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 227 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 228 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 229 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 230 231 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 232 233 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 234 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 235 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 236 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 237 238 **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a 239 lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: 240 241 - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, 242 summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change 243 without this repo hearing about it. 244 - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't 245 mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a 246 real defect there goes upstream instead. 247 - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry 248 **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is 249 `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. 250 251 None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose. 252

1	---
2	name: merge-and-ci
3	description: Drive this repo's PR-to-merged flow cheaply — when to open the PR, how to get CI green in a Claude web session, how to poll without wasting wall time or tokens, and when to arm auto-merge instead of waiting. Use whenever a session opens, watches, or lands a PR here — including one opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended or scheduled run, and any moment you ask "is CI green yet?" — not only for a deliberate merge or an e2e/heavy/UI change.
4	---
5	
6	# Merge and CI in this repo
7	
8	The merge itself: squash, `(#N)` appended to the title, CI green first (twice
9	for e2e/heavy-browser changes), approval-applies-only-backward — see the gcec
10	pack's RULES.md. This skill is the *how*: the environment facts and the poll
11	discipline that keep a merge cheap in wall time and tokens (from a post-mortem
12	on treating CI as a fixed poll-and-sleep ritual).
13	
14	## Open the PR early when the only reviewable output is on CI
15	
16	A change that adds or modifies an e2e/heavy-browser (`dev/requirements/heavy/`)
17	or UI-snapshot (`dev/requirements/{popup,icon}/`) test can't be exercised
18	locally — the sandbox has no Chrome — and its reviewable artifacts only exist
19	on a PR: CI runs the heavy/e2e suites against the branch, and a UI change's
20	reviewable output (the pixel diff GitHub renders, the inline gallery in the
21	branch's `dev/requirements/requirements.md`) needs a pushed branch to view at
22	all. Open the PR early for those.
23	
24	## Getting a green check in a Claude web session
25	
26	- **The push-run exists — don't dispatch a duplicate.** A push through the
27	  in-session git proxy **does** trigger `test.yml`: the workflow's `push`
28	  trigger covers `main` and `claude/**` precisely so an agent branch gets CI
29	  without a PR, and a branch that also has an open PR gets a `pull_request` run
30	  too (two `test` check runs on the same head SHA — the workflow's own comment
31	  calls that accepted duplication). Merge on whichever is green; only reach for
32	  `actions_run_trigger` / `run_workflow` when no run appeared at all (a branch
33	  outside `claude/**`, or a `paths-ignore`/`[skip ci]` push). Firing a manual
34	  dispatch on top of a run that already exists just buys a third run and its
35	  wall time.
36	- **The shell can't observe GitHub state here.** The git remote is a git-only
37	  proxy (smart-HTTP under `/git/<owner>/<repo>/…`; every other path 400s),
38	  there's no API token in the env, and `gh` reaches no `api.github.com` — only
39	  an MCP poll sees check state; a background bash/Monitor loop cannot.
40	- **Poll on a short back-off, never one long sleep, never tight.** Loop
41	  **MCP poll → background sleep → MCP poll** until the check leaves
42	  `in_progress`, backing off **5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, then 30s** repeating — a
43	  fast run wakes you within seconds, a slow one isn't tight-polled. Always wait
44	  for the sleep's completion notification before the next poll. While a sleep
45	  runs, do real work (review the diff, draft the PR body) or end the turn —
46	  filler calls to look busy are tight-polling in disguise.
47	- **Don't reach for `subscribe_pr_activity` to wait for green** — its webhooks
48	  never deliver CI **success** (only failures/comments/reviews), so the
49	  transition you're waiting for never arrives. It's for babysitting a PR, not
50	  merge-on-green.
51	- **Won't sit and poll to green? Arm auto-merge — never end a turn on a
52	  subscription.** A run that opens a PR it can't watch to the end (an
53	  unattended/scheduled run, or a fix opened incidentally mid-task) should
54	  `enable_pr_auto_merge` with `SQUASH` and finish: this repo's
55	  `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, so GitHub lands it the moment the
56	  checks pass, with no turn held open and no human in the loop. Ending the turn
57	  "waiting for CI events" instead strands the PR until a person notices —
58	  measured, in session `558026a0` (2026-07-24): both `test` runs were green at
59	  03:58:27Z, the turn had ended at 03:57:56Z on a `subscribe_pr_activity` watch,
60	  and PR #718 sat unmerged until the owner stepped in **63 minutes** later.
61	  That one avoidable wait was 85% of the session's 74-minute wall clock.
62	- **Batch tool loading**: one `ToolSearch` for every GitHub MCP tool the flow
63	  needs (`issue_write`, `create_pull_request`, `pull_request_read`,
64	  `merge_pull_request`), not one per turn.
65	
66	## After the merge, `git fetch origin main` — never check `main` out
67	
68	The canon merge recipe's post-merge step 5 is
69	`git checkout main && git pull origin main`. **Skip the checkout here**: a plain
70	`git fetch origin main` is all this repo's remaining post-merge work needs, and
71	the checkout is the one part that stalls or gets denied.
72	
73	Nothing downstream reads the working tree. The capture step that follows the
74	merge (`capture-log.mjs`) does every branch write through git plumbing against
75	the *fetched* remote tip and never touches the checkout or the index — its own
76	header says so. The conformance checks resolve their diff base from
77	`origin/main`, a remote-tracking ref a fetch alone advances. So the checkout
78	buys nothing but a working-tree switch nobody asked for, at the very end of a
79	session that is about to end anyway.
80	
81	Measured across the four captured sessions, all of which ran the canon step
82	verbatim: in `295e2230` (2026-07-26) the auto-mode classifier **denied**
83	`git checkout main` twice — once inside a `fetch && checkout && pull` chain
84	(08:26:09→08:26:39, 30s) and once alone (08:27:13→08:27:40, 27s) — 57s of dead
85	wall time plus three recovery calls, after which the session read the capture
86	script's header and concluded the checkout had never been needed. The bare
87	`git fetch origin main` in between succeeded on the first try. The same step
88	cost 44s in `13a6f736` and 8s in `558026a0` for no benefit either. Leave the
89	tree on the merged branch and fetch.
90

This refusal appears as a "delivery note" in the 2026-07-27 and 2026-07-30 entries above; this is its fourth occurrence and the first that produced a bad outcome, so it graduates from a note to a rule. The skill is the strongest mechanism available — no working-tree state at Stop time can observe an MCP call's return value.

- **Direct `curl` to `api.github.com` fails even with `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` in the env** ("GitHub access is not enabled for this session") — cost two Monitor loops started and stopped plus a failed JSON parse in `2925ea4b`.
